body: # Independent audit: two-contact slab transverse erosion gain `candidate 2bf98ea275da010b`. Result: **PASS**. No correction identified. ## Geometry and measures The single contact-interpolating fiber shear fixes the integer base, has continuous Jacobian one, and preserves every ambient halfspace. The individual signs b_+,b_->=0 follow from nonpositive critical cap margins at the other actual deepest point. The opposite unit continuous normals then give exactly the closed slab (1-z)J for z<1. Replacing the strict pair complement by this closed slab changes no d-volume: both boundaries have nonzero continuous normal. The transverse section E is a full (d-1)-dimensional body because the actual deepest point is interior to the positive fiber C_1. For z(t)=-t/(1-t), the coefficients (1-t)/(1-s) and (t-s)/(1-s) are positive and sum to one. Their base combination is exactly z(s). Actual fiber convexity therefore gives A_t+(t-s)C_1 subset A_s. Adding E consumes no u-coordinate, so the inclusion remains inside J and proves the stronger D_t inclusion. Nestedness uses only zero in E, not zero in any remote fiber. No projective change of the sampled measure is made. In dimension two, every nonempty transverse slice is an interval or singleton. Its sum with (t-s)E has exactly its old length plus (t-s)H_1(E). Integrating over the full projection interval proves (8), including a lower-dimensional D_t. The integer rescalings give exactly (j+1)^2 V_(j-1)-j^2 V_j>=j L w_j. Both the power two and the extra width factor j are correct. ## Concave moment estimate and all-dimensional constant For a nonnegative concave profile h, its endpoint-zero tent below a maximizer proves V>=w H^p/(p+1), hence A>=H. The superlevel lengths are concave in the level by Minkowski interpolation of intervals. A maximum plateau can produce a downward endpoint jump at H; this is compatible with concavity and does not invalidate the quotient argument. T-U starts at zero and has at most one positive-to-negative crossing. Equality of the p-moments is exactly the weighted integral identity (12). For 00; the source does not divide by them in the zero-volume cases. A nonempty zero-volume D_t of positive width still yields the separate a^p H_p(E)w bound by slice addition. Zero width supports no asserted positive d-volume gain. ## Genuine-contact sharpness The bipyramid product C=[-1,2] times K has exactly four positive integer fibers, each of mass W, and is full-dimensional. For a nonvertical cap through base0, the identical centrally symmetric fibers at -1 and1 contribute exactly W, its own fiber contributes W/2, and the fourth contributes nonnegatively. At base1 the pair is 0 and2. Pure integer closed containing caps have mass at least 2W, so positive boundary mass is handled correctly. The displayed pair has zero d-volume at the -1 supporting threshold, the middle-at-anchor contribution W/2, and paired contributions W at bases0 and2. Each displayed triple cap analogously has no positive volume at base2 and paired contributions W at -1 and1. The continuous triple normals positively balance, and its summed margin is a negative multiple of z. The pair covers z>=1 and the triple covers z<=0. Thus the five actual original caps cover every integer fiber and certify the matching global maximum 3W/2. Each fiber has mass W
